claim: Subacute stroke: higher alpha power than controls over central, parietal and occipital regions
detail: 57 subacute stroke patients (basal ganglia, fronto-temporal/centrum semiovale or brainstem lesions) and 22 matched controls, 5-minute eyes-open resting EEG with 128 channels. Alpha power was higher in patients, most strongly at the affected motor region (mapped to central sites), and peak alpha frequency was slower; the frontal region showed no alpha difference. Connectivity results are not used here, and beta results are not used because their direction was unclear. Case-control study.

cite.title: Lesion-specific EEG signatures in stroke: a multi-scale framework integrating oscillations, connectivity, and asymmetry for machine learning decoding

claim: OCD: more delta and theta power than controls in fronto-temporal and parietal regions
detail: 25 people with OCD and 27 healthy controls, eyes-closed resting EEG. Delta and theta power were higher in OCD in fronto-temporal and parietal regions; other bands and 1/f parameters showed no between-group difference. The reduced delta coherence is connectivity and is not used here. Taken from the abstract; not checked in the full text.

claim: LBD: less occipital alpha reactivity (eyes closed to open) than controls
detail: 41 people with Lewy body dementia, 21 with Alzheimer's and 40 controls, eyes-open and eyes-closed resting EEG. Alpha reactivity over O1, Oz and O2 was lower in LBD than in controls and lower than in AD; this came from higher eyes-open alpha power, while eyes-closed power did not differ from controls. Oz is recorded and mapped to O1 and O2. Cross-sectional case-control study.
